title: Dataverse tables of Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service: accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, quotes, orders, invoices with their lines, products and price lists, cases, users, teams, business units, currencies and activities
status_note: Written on 17 November 2026 from Microsoft Learn's table/column reference (every table's page was opened and its key, lookups and money columns checked, ms.date 2026-09-18) and the Learn pages on Azure Synapse Link and Link to Microsoft Fabric, in our own words. Table names are the logical names in upper case (SALESORDERDETAIL); columns are logical names read without case or underscores, and the Web API's _<name>_value spelling of a lookup is read as <name>. Not verified against any environment's rows: validate_plan does that on yours. Krusgraph is independent and not affiliated with Microsoft.

fabric_link.title: Link your Dataverse environment to Microsoft Fabric (Link to Microsoft Fabric)
fabric_link.note: Read 17 November 2026; ms.date 2026-07-06. Delta parquet replica in Dataverse storage, a lakehouse with shortcuts to the tables; all non-system tables with Track changes enabled are added; finance and operations tables can be linked too. The page does not say how lookup columns are named in the lakehouse.

fabric_link_platform.title: Link to Microsoft Fabric: how it works (latency, lakehouse naming, low-latency sync)
fabric_link_platform.note: Read 17 November 2026; ms.date 2026-11-11. Up to 60 minutes to update OneLake; the lakehouse name pattern is not to be relied on; low-latency sync writes timestamps as INT64.

synapse_link_columns.title: Azure Synapse Link: choose finance and operations data (the table of system columns: Id, IsDelete, SinkCreatedOn, SinkModifiedOn, versionnumber, sysrowversion)
synapse_link_columns.note: Read 17 November 2026; ms.date 2026-11-03. IsDelete true marks a soft-deleted row whose body is empty; SinkCreatedOn is when the row was written to the lake; versionnumber the last version synced. The page's sentence on reading active rows says to filter where isDelete is True, which reads as reversed; the FAQ (export_lake_faq) says isDeleted=0.

export_lake_faq.title: Azure Synapse Link for Dataverse: frequently asked questions
export_lake_faq.note: Read 17 November 2026; ms.date 2026-11-06. Deletes: appended row with isDeleted=True (append-only) or a soft delete and a hard delete after 30 days (Delta; the finance and operations page says 28); latest row by id with VersionNumber and SinkModifiedOn, then isDeleted=0; lookup columns are an id and a value: join to the table itself.

choice_labels.title: Azure Synapse Link: access choice labels (OptionsetMetadata, GlobalOptionsetMetadata, StateMetadata, StatusMetadata, TargetMetadata)
choice_labels.note: Read 17 November 2026; ms.date 2022-04-27. A choice column holds the number; the label is in OptionsetMetadata (EntityName, OptionSetName, Option, LocalizedLabelLanguageCode, LocalizedLabel). TargetMetadata lists each lookup (AttributeName, e.g. transactioncurrencyid) with its ReferencedEntity: the only statement read that names a lookup column in the lake by its logical name.

tables.name: ACCOUNT
tables.en: Account (a company the organisation does business with)
tables.note: Key ACCOUNTID (a GUID); name column NAME. PARENTACCOUNTID is the parent account, PRIMARYCONTACTID the primary contact. In the lakehouse that Link to Microsoft Fabric creates, the table carries the system columns of Azure Synapse Link (Id, IsDelete, SinkCreatedOn, SinkModifiedOn, versionnumber); read only rows where IsDelete is not true.

tables.name: CONTACT
tables.note: Key CONTACTID; name column FULLNAME. PARENTCUSTOMERID is a Customer lookup: an account or a contact, with PARENTCUSTOMERIDTYPE saying which. Personal data throughout.

amounts.currency: TRANSACTIONCURRENCYID (a lookup to transactioncurrency); each money column has a _BASE twin in the organisation's base currency, converted with EXCHANGERATE

tables.note: Key LEADID; name column FULLNAME. Qualifying a lead creates an opportunity: QUALIFYINGOPPORTUNITYID on the lead, ORIGINATINGLEADID on the opportunity. CUSTOMERID is a Customer lookup (account or contact).

TRANSACTIONCURRENCYID (a lookup to transactioncurrency); each money column has a _BASE twin in the organisation's base currency, converted with EXCHANGERATE

tables.name: ACTIVITYPOINTER

traps.title: Header totals and line amounts are the same money
traps.text: OPPORTUNITY.ESTIMATEDVALUE and TOTALAMOUNT, QUOTE.TOTALAMOUNT, SALESORDER.TOTALAMOUNT and INVOICE.TOTALAMOUNT are totals of their products (with discounts, freight and tax); OPPORTUNITYPRODUCT, QUOTEDETAIL, SALESORDERDETAIL and INVOICEDETAIL.EXTENDEDAMOUNT are the lines. Summing a header total over a join with its lines counts it once per line; adding header and line amounts counts the order twice. Sum the lines, or the headers alone.

traps.title: Pipeline, quotes, orders and invoices are four stages of one sale
traps.text: A won opportunity becomes a quote, an order and an invoice, each with its own total (QUOTEID, OPPORTUNITYID and SALESORDERID link them). Adding ESTIMATEDVALUE of opportunities to TOTALAMOUNT of orders or invoices counts the same sale more than once; ACTUALVALUE defaults to ESTIMATEDVALUE when the opportunity is won, so it is a forecast figure until someone corrects it.

traps.title: Deleted rows stay in the lake with IsDelete
traps.text: Azure Synapse Link and Link to Microsoft Fabric keep a deleted row as a soft delete (IsDelete true, an empty body) until it is purged after about 30 days (28 on one page), and append-only tables add a row per change. Filter IsDelete and, for append-only tables, keep the latest row per id by versionnumber and SinkModifiedOn before counting or summing. SinkCreatedOn is when the lake got the row, not when the record was created (CREATEDON).

traps.title: Customer, owner and regarding lookups point at more than one table
traps.text: CUSTOMERID and PARENTCUSTOMERID hold an account or a contact, OWNERID a user or a team, REGARDINGOBJECTID any of a long list of tables. A join of the column to one table finds nothing for the rows that point at another: filter on the type column (CUSTOMERIDTYPE, PARENTCUSTOMERIDTYPE, OWNERIDTYPE, REGARDINGOBJECTTYPECODE) first. The pack lists one filtered relationship per target table; none is a plain key join.

traps.title: A lookup has a different name in the Web API and in the lake
traps.text: The Web API returns a lookup as _<name>_value (_parentaccountid_value), a computed GUID; the table reference names the column by its logical name (parentaccountid), which is also how TargetMetadata in the lake names it (AttributeName). The pack reads both spellings. That the Fabric lakehouse names every lookup column by its logical name is stated on no page read: confirm it on your tables.

traps.title: Choice columns hold numbers; the labels are in metadata tables
traps.text: STATECODE, STATUSCODE and every choice column hold a number. The label is in OptionsetMetadata, GlobalOptionsetMetadata, StateMetadata and StatusMetadata (by EntityName, OptionSetName, Option and the language code): join on all of them, or a label in another language doubles the rows.

traps.title: Every money column is in the record's own currency
traps.text: Money columns are in the currency of TRANSACTIONCURRENCYID; the _BASE twin is in the organisation's base currency, converted with the record's EXCHANGERATE. Summing EXTENDEDAMOUNT across currencies adds kronor to euros: sum EXTENDEDAMOUNT_BASE, or group by currency.
